name: The Ancestor's Knucklebone
object: A knucklebone worn smooth by a hundred years of handling, threaded on gut string. Taken from the body of a Berserker who died fighting in the Borderlands and was never retrieved. It arrived in a collector's satchel through one of the Market Square arches, and nobody knows which world it came from, or who carried it through.
unlock: Defeat an enemy in single combat without any ally's assistance.
Keep one of the body's hand bones.
Spend a night alone with it before you sleep, and see how the ancestor fought.
risk: Whatever hunted the ancestor still wants the bone, and the night alone is when it finds you.

resource.name: Fury Echo
resource.text: Fury Echo (pip tracker, max 3). Gain 1 Fury Echo each time you tell a listener who has not heard it how the ancestor fought and fell, in full, over at least ten minutes. Echo never clears at a rest or when combat ends. Spent Echo returns only by telling it again to a new listener.

powers: Echo Strike (Free, while Raging, spend 1 Fury Echo): Roll a Fury Die and set it aside with the rest, up to your maximum. This does not use your Rage action.
Death's Door (Free, 1/encounter, when you Rage, spend all 3 Fury Echo): For this encounter, your Rage does not end when you drop to 0 HP. Dying applies as normal.
escalation: If you drop to 0 HP with Death's Door active, the knucklebone cracks and stops working. Replace it with another ancestor's relic from the Borderlands, or take one from a worthy enemy. The GM decides where it is and how long the search takes. Whatever hunted the ancestor learns the bone has moved.
design_note: Echo comes from a story told at a table, so the pool fills outside the fight and never from the Fury Dice the class already rolls. Death's Door is paid at the start of Rage, before the dangerous moment, and gives a first-echelon version of the level 18 Deep Rage.
notes: Reworked. Echo now fills by retelling, not by Fury Die matches (double-dipping); Death's Door paid up front (peak-value lethality); risk added; em dash removed; retelling venue: Sevenge and Gam's Public House (3_gazetteer).

matrix.refill: Tell the ancestor's last fight to a listener who has not heard it; persists until spent
matrix.cost: Echo spent; relic cracks at 0 HP with Death's Door
matrix.origin: Borderlands Berserker relic, arrived via a Market Square arch (world unnamed)

name: The Loaded Die
object: An ivory gambling die with a tiny lead insert that makes it land on 6 roughly two-thirds of the time. Confiscated from a Black Hand card sharp at the Lower Reaches gambling house, then stolen from the evidence shelf at the Golden Knights' outpost. No paperwork exists for it. The card sharp has not stopped looking.
unlock: Win a wager against someone who genuinely believed they had the advantage: not a mark, not a fool, but someone who should have won.
Stake something you cannot afford to lose.
risk: The Black Hand card sharp hears whose hands the die is in.

resource.name: Fixes
resource.text: Fixes (pip tracker, max 4). Fixes do not refill automatically. To refill: run a game of chance during a Safe Rest and earn at least 1 silver in genuine winnings against an opponent who had a real chance of winning. Gain all 4 Fixes back. Safe Rests where you do not gamble leave the tracker as it is.

powers: Fix (Free, before you roll, spend 1 Fix): Declare you are using the die. Roll your Primary Die twice and take whichever result you prefer. No memory required, both rolls happen now, in front of everyone.
Loaded Odds (Passive): Once per session, you may ask the GM whether a creature you can see is bluffing. The die rolls and the GM answers truthfully, but only yes or no.
escalation: When all 4 Fixes are spent, the die gets you anyway. On your next Vicious Opportunist use after depletion, the GM secretly decides whether the target was actually Distracted, and you do not know until after you have committed. The uncertainty lasts for one use only. Word that a loaded die is back in play reaches the card sharp within a session.
design_note: Mirrors Vicious Opportunist's loop of manipulating die results, but at a resource cost. Roll twice, pick best, needs no memory. Loaded Odds is social utility that costs nothing in stats. The escalation adds uncertainty for a class that is normally certain about when it cheats, and a pursuer.
notes: Risk line and a costly unlock step added; em dashes removed; escalation now brings the card sharp back. Left: Loaded Odds overlaps the Insight skill (detect lies); kept as free social utility per the spec.

matrix.refill: Run a game of chance during a Safe Rest and win 1 sp from a real opponent
matrix.origin: Black Hand card sharp, Lower Reaches gambling house; Golden Knights evidence shelf

name: The Battle Standard of the Nameless King
object: A black iron battle standard, the insignia ground off but the pole still bearing ghost-traces of a name no one can read. Found stacked with other confiscated relics in the Museum of Worlds Beyond storage vault. The curator is looking for it. Three scholars have separately attempted to identify the insignia's origin and stopped work without explanation.
unlock: Lead a group of at least five non-party combatants to victory: soldiers, militia, hired swords, anyone you commanded in the field. The victory must be real, a fight that could have been lost.
Plant the standard yourself, in plain sight of the enemy.
risk: The Knights of the Nameless King learn that this standard flies again.

resource.name: Authority
resource.text: Authority (pip tracker, max 3). Gain 1 Authority whenever an ally within 4 spaces of the planted standard deals damage in a single attack equal to or greater than your level. Authority is strictly encounter-bound: all unspent pips are lost when combat ends, regardless of how many are held. It cannot be saved or stockpiled between encounters.

powers: Plant it (1 Action): Drive the standard into the ground within Reach 1. While it stands, allies within 4 spaces who can see it have advantage on their first attack each round. Spend 1 Authority to extend the aura by 2 spaces until your next turn.
Pull it (Free): The standard returns to your hand and the aura ends immediately.
Hold Ground (Reaction, spend 2 Authority): When the standard would be knocked over, stolen, or destroyed, it refuses. It cannot be moved by any force until the start of your next turn.
escalation: When Authority is at 0 during combat and you plant the standard anyway, the insignia becomes briefly legible to everyone present. The GM reads what it says aloud. It goes dark again immediately. What it says is the GM's tool: a name, a title, a command. Prepare it before the session.
design_note: Authority triggers on a damage threshold, not on defeats, so no ally gains by stealing last hits. Any solid hit fills the pool, which rewards coordinated pressure. The escalation is pure City of Arches: the Nameless King's name appears once, and only the GM knows what it says.
notes: Risk line and a costly unlock step added; aura range stated in the resource line; em dashes removed. Left: Authority fills from allies' damage and clears at encounter end, so it has no world refill. This is the spec's own example of a good Commander item.

matrix.refill: Gained when an ally in the aura deals damage of at least your level; lost at encounter end
matrix.origin: Nameless King relic from the Museum of Worlds Beyond vault

name: The Borderlands Tracking Cord
object: A length of braided sinew hung with small carved tokens: a boot print, a feather, a fang, and three others worn unrecognisable by handling. Carried by a tracker from the Doorish Hills who traded it to a Lower Reaches merchant for safe passage through the Cliffs of the Dead. The merchant did not survive the arrangement.
unlock: Track a single creature across at least two sessions without losing the trail, through city, ruin, or wilderness. The creature must be aware it is being hunted, and must have tried to lose you at least once.
risk: The creature you tracked now knows your trail as well as you know theirs.

resource.name: Marks
resource.text: Marks (d6 vs. accumulation). Your Mark count is the number of quarries the cord currently tracks. Roll 1d6 each time you use a cord ability (Mark a Quarry or Cord Pull). If you roll equal to or below your current Mark count, something near the quarry noticed you. A Mark clears when you confront that quarry directly or when you Cut its Mark. Resting does not clear Marks.

powers: Mark a Quarry (1 Action): Touch the cord to any physical trace of a creature: a footprint, a drop of blood, shed skin. Add 1 Mark. While that quarry is marked, you know its general direction and distance within 1 mile regardless of cover or concealment. This works on creatures you have not marked with Hunter's Mark, because the cord marks independently of the class ability.
Cord Pull (Free, 1/encounter): When your marked quarry moves away from you, pull the cord taut. The quarry is Slowed. No roll required. The quarry feels it.

Cut the Mark (Free): Remove one Mark from the cord and burn its token. The cord forgets that quarry, your sense of its direction ends, and it is no longer tracked. Use this when the pursuit is no longer worth the rising risk. Nothing alerts the quarry.
escalation: When the d6 roll triggers, the quarry, or something near it, begins tracking you in return. The GM introduces this threat within 1 to 2 sessions. The threat is proportional to what you marked: a city rat sends a rat, a Borderlands warlord sends soldiers.
design_note: The d6 tracker suits the Hunter's quarry identity. Several Marks make each use riskier, so tracking three creatures at once invites trouble. The cord works beyond sight, which Hunter's Mark does not. Being tracked back is the most Hunter-specific consequence available.
notes: Marks now one count with one clearing rule (confront or Cut); Safe Rest wipe removed; risk line added; em dashes removed; Slowed uses the rules wording.

matrix.refill: Marks clear when you confront the quarry or Cut its Mark
matrix.origin: Doorish Hills tracker, traded to a Lower Reaches merchant, via the Cliffs of the Dead

name: The Cracked Lens of Kartan
object: A monocle lens of blue glass, cracked through the centre but held in a copper frame that prevents the crack from spreading. Stamped with the Mages of Kartan's maker's mark on the inner rim. The Mages report it stolen. It has been in a Lower Reaches pawn shop for six months, priced too high for anyone who recognised it, too strange for anyone who didn't.
unlock: Pay the pawn shop's price, which is more than the lens is worth.
Cast a spell of the highest tier you can cast, and hold the lens against your eye through the whole cast without flinching or removing it.
risk: If you flinch, the crack spreads and the lens is ruined.

resource.name: Overcharge
resource.text: Overcharge (d6 vs. accumulation). Roll 1d6 each time you cast a tiered spell while wearing the lens. If you roll equal to or below your current Overcharge, the lens fails (see Escalation). Overcharge clears when you hold the lens to the glass of the Observatory of Infinite Skies through one night.

powers: Controlled Upcast (while worn, on a safe roll, Control subclass only): When you cast a tiered spell and the d6 does not trigger, the spell gains one Upcast for free. Add 1 Overcharge. Chaos subclass: no upcast. On a safe roll, reduce Overcharge by 1 (minimum 0).

Chaos Sight (Passive, while worn): You see magical auras on creatures and objects within 4 spaces without casting a spell. Illusions appear slightly wrong. Invisible creatures show as a faint shimmer.
escalation: When the d6 triggers, the glass heats to burning. Control Mage: you Lose Control, doing every option on the Control Table, with the GM choosing each time. Chaos Mage: you Invoke Chaos with disadvantage. Either way you take 1 Wound and cannot remove the lens until the encounter ends, because it has fused to your face. After the encounter, the Mages of Kartan sense the discharge and know its rough location. They send someone within 1 to 3 sessions. The fusing is now, the visitors are later.
design_note: Differentiated by subclass. The Control Mage gets a free Upcast on safe rolls, a reward for precision, and Lose Control as the failure. The Chaos Mage gets Overcharge relief on safe rolls and a worse Chaos roll on failure. Neither subclass wins both ways. The Mages of Kartan escalation is the City of Arches hook.
notes: Failure now matches the Mage rules (Control mages Lose Control, Chaos mages Invoke Chaos); the 'Control roll' unlock replaced; refill changed from abstention plus rest to a night at the Observatory; costly step and risk added. [NEEDS CANON: whether the Observatory of Infinite Skies lets a visitor leave a lens at its glass overnight.]

matrix.refill: Hold the lens to the Observatory of Infinite Skies glass for a night
matrix.origin: Mages of Kartan maker's mark; Lower Reaches pawn shop; Observatory of Infinite Skies

name: The Broken Verdict
object: A set of golden scales, one pan snapped off and missing. Recovered from the rubble of an old court in the ruins of Sunken Revvia. The remaining pan still tilts when a lie is spoken nearby, or so the merchant who sold it claimed. She may have been lying. The tilt is subtle enough that you cannot always be certain.
unlock: Refuse to deliver a verdict you believe is just, because doing so would protect someone you love.
The refusal must be genuine. The Verdict will know if you were simply afraid.
risk: Whoever was owed the verdict now knows you withheld it.

resource.name: Held Judgment
resource.text: Held Judgment (toggle, on/off). When your Radiant Judgment would roll Judgment Dice, you may put them on the scales instead (toggle on). While the scales hold dice, you roll no new Judgment Dice. Held dice stay on the scales past the end of the encounter. The toggle clears when you Release the dice on an attack, or when you perform a Sacred Decree (see Escalation).

powers: Hold Judgment (Free, when Judgment Dice would be rolled): Keep the dice on the scales. While they are held, you see the remaining pan tilt when a creature within 6 spaces lies to you, visible only to you. You know. They do not know you know. You must decide what to do with that.
Release (Free, 1/encounter, on a Reach attack): Expend the held dice as Radiant Judgment normally does. This attack's radiant damage ignores armor.
escalation: If the scales hold dice through a full Safe Rest, they fuse with your Lay on Hands pool. You cannot spend from the pool until you perform a Sacred Decree at the Temple of the Three Sisters. The temple will want to know why.
design_note: Every time Judgment Dice would roll, the player chooses between spending them on the next attack and holding them for an armor-ignoring release. Holding is paid before the dangerous moment, and the lie-detection stays one-sided, so social scenes become dramatic irony.
notes: Rewritten to fit the Oathsworn rules: Judgment Dice are not spent on reactions (the 'That All You Got?!' line was a Berserker ability) and expire at the end of the encounter, so the card now states that held dice persist. Origin reworded from 'Magistrate's Court in the Sunken Revvia district'. [NEEDS CANON: a court in the ruins of Sunken Revvia; setting/7_sunken_revvia.md names none.] Risk added.

matrix.refill: Toggle on when Judgment Dice would roll; Release on an attack or perform a Sacred Decree
matrix.cost: Lay on Hands locked until a Sacred Decree
matrix.origin: Sunken Revvia court ruin [NEEDS CANON]; Temple of the Three Sisters

name: The Hollow Contract
object: A slip of black vellum the size of a playing card, written in a language that changes every time you look away. No ink is visible: the text appears to be burned into the material from within. Found pressed between the floorboards of a sealed room in the Lower Reaches, below a building that has been empty for eleven years. The landlord will not say why.
unlock: Patron path: commune with your patron during a Safe Rest and ask it for something you know it does not want to give. Accept its counter-demand before you know what it is.
Reaver path: you have no patron to ask. Read the vellum by your own shadow, in the room where it was found, until the language stops changing.
risk: Your patron, or the patron you left, learns the contract has a new reader.

resource.name: Debt
resource.text: Debt (pip tracker, max 4). Mark 1 Debt each time you use one of the contract's powers. Debt clears when the patron collects (see Escalation), or when you carry out a sentence you wrote in the contract: write one sentence in your own blood describing something you will do for the patron, then do it. You must write something real, and you must mean it.

powers: Read the Contract (Free, 1/encounter, mark 1 Debt): Hold the vellum up. You see one true fact about a creature you can see: its most urgent want, its deepest fear, or the name of someone it has wronged.
Patron's Margin (Free, 1/encounter, mark 2 Debt, patron path): Cast one tiered spell you know at +1 tier above your current maximum. The patron extends credit.
Reaver's Margin (Free, 1/encounter, mark 2 Debt, Reaver path): Your next Bonescythe strike this turn rolls 1 extra damage die.
escalation: When Debt reaches 4, the patron collects. It does not take power. It adds one sentence about your character to the contract, permanently. The GM decides what it says and reads it aloud. Debt clears. The sentence stays. A Reaver's former patron sends an agent to read the sentence to them in person.
design_note: Debt marks only on the contract's own powers, so it never rides on Pilfered Power, and the Safe Rest commune stays the class's own business. The Reaver path gives patronless Shadowmancers a card of their own. The permanent sentence is the right shape for a relationship with something ancient and dangerous.
notes: Debt no longer marks on Pilfered Power use and the Pilfered Power refill is gone (it duplicated the class commune); Reaver path and Reaver's Margin added (Reavers have no patron and cannot cast tiered spells at this echelon); risk added; em dash removed.

matrix.refill: Carry out a sentence written in blood for the patron (or the patron left)
matrix.cost: narrative: patron writes a sentence on you
matrix.origin: Lower Reaches, sealed room under an empty building

name: The Bell of the Three Sisters
object: A small iron handbell, tarnished green at the rim, engraved with three interlinked rings. Identical to the bells carried by the clergy of the Temple of the Three Sisters, except that this one rings slightly differently, a half-note flat or sharp depending on who you ask. The temple says it was never consecrated. They are interested in recovering it for study. They have not offered to pay.
unlock: Heal a creature you expected, and had good reason, to be your enemy. The expectation must be genuine. The bell listens.
risk: The temple learns that a stranger carries a bell it never consecrated.

resource.name: Resonance
resource.text: Resonance (pip tracker, max 4). Gain 1 Resonance by ringing the bell for an hour over a sickbed or a grave, at the Temple of the Three Sisters or among the tombs of the Cliffs of the Dead, and staying with whoever it is for until the hour ends. Resonance does not clear at a rest. Spent Resonance returns only this way.

powers: Ring (Free, when you heal HP): The bell tones as you heal. Undead within 4 spaces take 1 radiant damage.

Chain Heal (Reaction, spend 2 Resonance): When your Lifebinding Spirit heals a creature to maximum HP, the excess healing carries to the nearest damaged ally within 4 spaces. The chain triggers once per Reaction.
Toll (1 Action, spend all 4): Ring the bell loudly. All Dying allies within 6 spaces gain 1 HP and are no longer Dying. You take 1 Wound.
escalation: Spending all 4 Resonance in the Toll cracks the bell's handle. It still rings, but you cannot Toll until a clergyperson of the Three Sisters rehandles it. They will want to know what happened before they agree to help.
design_note: Every power keys off healing, and none of the pool fills from healing, so it adds to the Shepherd's rhythm without rewarding it twice. Chain Heal makes positioning the Spirit a puzzle. The Toll is a first-echelon rescue that costs a Wound and permanently marks the bell. Sacrifice should have weight.
notes: Resonance now fills by ringing over a sickbed or grave (it filled from Searing Light, the class's own move, and Searing Light does not heal: it damages a target for HP you heal). Unlock reworded to 'heal'. Ring no longer gives the Spirit an extra action. Resonance persists through rests. Risk added.

matrix.refill: Ring the bell for an hour over a sickbed or grave, staying with them
matrix.look: iron handbell, green rim, three rings

name: The Theater of Whispers Setlist
object: A folded sheet of vellum with a handwritten set of songs: titles, keys, and performance notes in the margins in an elegant hand. It belonged to a Songweaver who performed at the Theater of Whispers for fifteen years before disappearing mid-run. The theater kept the setlist. Someone stole it last month. The manager has posted a reward, but is vaguer than expected about what they want to do with whoever took it.
unlock: Perform at the Theater of Whispers, or any venue with an audience of 20 or more, and hold the crowd's full attention for an uninterrupted hour. No skill check. Just perform.
risk: Someone in that crowd knows the hand that wrote the setlist.

resource.name: Crowd
resource.text: Crowd (d6 vs. accumulation, max 4). Each time you Call the Song in combat, roll 1d6 against your current Crowd, then add 1 Crowd. If you roll equal to or below your Crowd before adding, someone recognises the song and has feelings about it: you have disadvantage on your next social roll with a stranger this session. Crowd clears when you play a full uninterrupted hour for a new audience of 20 or more.

powers: Call the Song (Free, in combat, 1/round): Name the song you are playing and roll against your Crowd. On a safe roll, you regain 1 spent use of Songweaver's Inspiration. This works once per encounter.
Protective Verse (Free, 1/encounter, remove 2 Crowd): A specific song from the setlist grants immunity to the Taunted or Frightened condition to all allies within 6 spaces until the end of the round.
escalation: When Crowd reaches 4, someone in the crowd knows who this setlist belonged to. They approach between encounters, or send someone. The GM decides who and what they want. They may be a fan. They may not.
design_note: Crowd is soft pressure: accumulating rarely hurts until 4, and a failed roll is a light social tax. Call the Song extends Songweaver's Inspiration with a mid-encounter refill. The escalation connects to the missing Songweaver, a mystery the GM can develop at any pace.
notes: 'Theatre' corrected to 'Theater' (3_gazetteer); the per-ally, per-session cap (memory tracking) replaced with once per encounter; Songweaver's Inspiration belongs to the Songweaver, so the refill now returns the Songweaver's own uses; Crowd clears by a full hour for a new audience (was a Safe Rest); risk added.

matrix.refill: Play a full uninterrupted hour for a new audience of 20 or more

name: Mud from the Revlend Marshes
object: A sealed clay jar of dark grey mud from the Revlend Marshes north of the city, marked with protective runes no one recognises as any known system. The mud is warm to the touch and smells of rain before a storm. It never dries out. An arch-traveller carried it into the city claiming the marshes spoke to her. She didn't explain further. She is not currently available to explain anything.
unlock: Spend a full night alone in the Revlend Marshes, or in the Deadlands adjacent to them, without shelter or fire.
Something in the marshes must acknowledge you before dawn. You will know if it did.
risk: Whatever acknowledges you now knows your name.

resource.name: Earthpulse
resource.text: Earthpulse (pip tracker, max 4). The jar holds 4 Earthpulse when it is full. Using the mud spends Earthpulse (see Powers). Spent Earthpulse returns only when you carry the jar back to the Revlend Marshes and leave it there overnight. A rest does not refill it.

powers: Apply (1 Action, spend 1 Earthpulse): Smear the mud on yourself or a willing creature. While it is applied, the creature cannot be pushed, thrown, or moved by non-magical forced movement. Mud washes off in rain or after a Field Rest.
Extend the Beastshift (Free, spend 2 Earthpulse, once per Beastshift): Your Beastshift does not end when you cast a spell this encounter.

Mire (1 Action, spend all 4): Create a 3-space radius of difficult terrain centered on you that lasts until the end of the encounter. The ground thickens and pulls. Any creature that starts its turn in the mire is Slowed.
escalation: When the jar is empty, mud already applied does not dry, but no new mud can be applied until the jar is refilled. If the jar breaks, the mud it held dries at once and all its effects end. A skilled craftsperson can repair a broken jar, but the marshes must still refill it. Each time you return to refill it, the marshes have changed, and the GM says how.
design_note: The geographic refill anchors the item in the setting. Every use is a conscious spend of a resource that costs a journey to replace, and no use refills it. Extend the Beastshift answers the class's own tension of forms ending when you cast. Mire gives battlefield control that fits the nature identity without requiring more spellcasting.
notes: Self-sustaining loop removed: Apply used to give Earthpulse, which paid for the other powers; it now costs 1. 'Shift ability' and 'storm form' replaced with Beastshift (rules: it ends when you cast a spell); risk added; the marshes change on each return.

matrix.refill: Carry the jar back to the Revlend Marshes and leave it overnight
matrix.look: sealed clay jar of grey mud

name: The Pain Teacher's Wrappings
object: Linen hand wrappings, yellowed and stained, covered in faded ink annotations, technique notes in a script that predates the city. Found in a locked case in the Lower Reaches beneath a martial arts studio that has been occupied by different teachers for four centuries. Each teacher added their own notes in the margins. The last teacher's annotations stop mid-sentence, mid-technique.
unlock: Take a hit in combat that you could have Defended but deliberately chose not to, in order to observe how the attack was made. The choice must be your own. The wrappings can tell the difference between courage and negligence.
risk: The last teacher's notes stop mid-technique, and whoever silenced them hears the wrappings are in use.

resource.name: Strain
resource.text: Strain (Wound-cost). Each annotation you use costs 1 Wound. There is no tracker, only the Wounds. They heal as Wounds normally do, 1 per Safe Rest.

powers: Study the Form (Free, spend 1 Wound, 1/encounter): Before you attack a creature, spend 1 Wound to activate the wrappings' oldest annotations. For the rest of the encounter, your attacks against that creature ignore its armor. You are choosing to hurt yourself to learn faster.
Deepest Annotation (Free, spend 1 Wound, 1/Safe Rest): Your unarmed and martial weapon attacks deal bonus damage equal to your level for 1 minute.

Study (downtime, 1 hour per Safe Rest): Spend an hour reading the annotations during rest. Roll Lore DC 8 to learn something about a martial tradition relevant to the current adventure arc. The GM provides one true detail.
escalation: If you use either annotation while you have 3 or more Wounds, from any source, the wrappings tighten around your hands: take 1 additional Wound and you cannot use either annotation for 1 round. The annotations become illegible until a skilled martial artist re-inks them. Finding one is the GM's hook.
design_note: The Wound is paid before the attack, so you choose when the risk comes, not the enemy. Armor-ignore proves most useful against heavily armored foes, and you pay for it in advance. Way of Pain players will recognise the trade immediately.
notes: Escalation could not fire (it needed three uses of a 1/Safe Rest power); it now fires on using an annotation at 3 or more Wounds, a value readable now. 'Cannot be healed until Safe Rest' removed (Wounds already heal 1 per Safe Rest). Study relabelled downtime. Risk added.

matrix.refill: None; Wounds from Strain heal on Safe Rest

name: The Forgotten Key
object: A tarnished iron key, not sized for any human lock. Its bow is etched with a spiral that matches no arch in the city's records.
unlock: Present it to each of the city's seven major arches while the Archkeepers watch
Find the one arch that hums
Spend a full night at its threshold
risk: The arch opens briefly, and something may come through before you close it.

resource.name: Resonance
resource.text: Resonance (3). Mark when you open an arch, clear on a Safe Rest.

powers: Open the Way (Action, 1 Resonance): a dormant arch opens for up to a minute. Lore DC 12, or you can't control where it leads. A crit lets you sense the destination first.
escalation: Spending the last Resonance, roll d6. On 1-2 the key splinters, and every arch it opens leads somewhere wrong until an Archkeeper repairs it. On 3+, take 1 Wound.

object: A cold, clammy pendant, a single shimmering scale of unknown origin. Everyone nearby shivers when it is first worn.
unlock: See the homebrew document

object: A silvery greataxe with nine open eyes engraved down the blade. They follow whoever speaks.
unlock: Learn what the axe was called before it was named, from Archkeeper records or something older than the Golden Order
Let it name a creature in a room you thought was empty
Hold the line against that creature until it flees or dies
risk: The creature's side now knows your name.

resource.name: Eyes
resource.text: Eyes (9). A closed eye never reopens.

escalation: Named creatures learn your name and heading each dawn. When the ninth eye closes, the axe speaks your True Name and all nine hear it. One engraved eye is scraped blank.

name: The Hourglass of Borrowed Time
object: A brass hourglass whose sand climbs upward.
unlock: Watch one full night without sleeping
Tell an NPC, truthfully, the moment you would undo
risk: The sand climbs for a stranger first. They relive their last hour, and they remember you.

resource.name: Sand
resource.text: Sand (3). Regain 1 by returning to where you last turned time back and letting the glass run for an hour.

powers: Turn Back (Reaction, 1 Sand): any die roll you can see is rerolled. The new result stands.

name: The Black Lotus Case
object: A black bloom pressed in a lead-lined case, three petals left, still damp.
unlock: Find someone who survived the preparation
Fast three days
Eat the first petal under watch
risk: WIL DC 14 or take 2 Wounds, and the Stain advances now.

resource.name: Petals
